title: Backing Sam Cooke for Don Robey and learning of his death
summary: Robey's office hires Fields' band for Sam Cooke dates after Rene Hall vouches for him; on the road in West Texas he hears Cooke was shot, ending that hope for Junior.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: What I meant is I was usually looked on as Ernie Fields and Son, but the time that Sam Cooke was killed, I was--I just opened a tour with him, and to show you how hard it is (inaudible).

bought some dates on Sam Cooke, twelve or fifteen, and he wanted a band to back him and somehow or another my name came up and Evelyn Johnson, his secretary had contacted me and I told her yes. I had done work for them before but after all, they wanted to get their own opinion, and they said something to Sam Cooke, did he know anything about Ernie Fields' band and Sam said, not particularly, but Rene used to be in his band, maybe he could say something, but that was years ago.

So they gave Rene Hall a call and wanted to know did he think Ernie Field's band could play Sam Cooke's music. Rene turned (inaudible). To tell you the truth, I don't know what Ernie has, but if he has a band, he'll play his book.

So I got those dates and did so well that they were planning another one at that time, and we were out, on the highway, I'll never forget, I was out in West Texas, was headed to Midland, Texas where we were
together one time. I was going in there, we were going to play the Country Club, and incidentally, those are some repeats that I was making that originally Reg Marshall had booked me in there.

On the way we were travelling in two cars and a trailer pulling the instruments and one of the cars had on their radio and they were in front and they stopped and flagged us down and they said did you listen to the radio. I said what happened? They said it just came on that Sam Cooke was shot. That was really a blow, because (inaudible), and at that time I was trying to build Junior and if we had made that last tour, we were going to be saying something about him.
That was about my last years from the band.
But you did play some country club dates?
That's Spurgeon, Luther West and then one of your men there, Harry.
(Side A of Tape 6 ends at this point. Transcript will continue with Side B.)
